title: Jhon Duran joins Zenit St. Petersburg on loan from Al Nassr
content:
Colombia striker Jhon Duran has completed a loan move to Zenit St. Petersburg from Al Nassr.

The move sees the 22-year-old join the sixth club of his senior career, and represents his fourth different club in the space of just over a year.

Duran will spend the remainder of the 2025-26 campaign at the Russian club, having cut short his season-long loan at Fenerbahce.

He joined Fenerbahce in the summer and made 21 appearances in all competitions for the Turkish club, scoring five goals and providing three assists.

Duran old joined Al Nassr for a €77million (£64.5m) fee plus add-ons from Aston Villa in the 2025 January transfer window, signing a five-and-a-half year contract with the club.

The Colombia international scored 12 goals in 18 appearances as Al Nassr finished 13 points off champions Al Ittihad in the Saudi Pro League, before moving to Fenerbahce in the summer.

He came through the academy at Envigado in Colombia before joining Major League Soccer team Chicago Fire in January 2021. Two years later, he signed for Aston Villa for a fee of up to £17.75m. He was mainly used as back-up behind starting striker Ollie Watkins, and scored 20 goals in 78 Villa appearances.

Duran was the subject of interest from West Ham United in the summer of 2024, with Villa rejecting an offer for him. West Ham made another bid of £57m in January last year which was also rejected before he eventually joined Al Nassr.

The striker made his senior debut for Colombia in September 2022 and has been capped 17 times at international level, scoring three goals.

Zenit are second in the Russian Premier League, one point behind league leaders Krasnodar. Russian sides have been suspended from competing in UEFA competitions since the country’s illegal, full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
